generatedProse.concept-context: Work across the School of Sport swings between the two modes all the time. Planning a coaching session starts divergent: a coach brainstorms the drills a session could use, including awkward ones. Then it turns convergent: they weigh the drills against the players, the time and the goal, and choose. The same split runs through a sport scientist shortlisting test protocols or a manager sifting event ideas. Running both at once, judging each idea as it occurs, tends to leave you with the first safe option and little else.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching students plan the same training session, with twenty minutes before the seminar.

Tom picks a drill straight away and starts writing the plan, judging each choice as it comes. Twenty minutes later there is half a session mapped, each drill swapped twice. Tom ran both modes at once, generating and judging in the same breath, so little was generated and less survived.

Amara spends the first ten minutes listing every drill that might fit the session goal, good and bad, without stopping to judge. Then, in the second ten, she reads the list, crosses out the weak ones, and picks the two that build into a progression. Generating first and choosing second gave her more to work with, and a stronger plan.

Both had the same twenty minutes. Only Amara kept the two modes apart, which let the ideas flow and then settle.
generatedProse.summary: In the School of Sport, creative thinking uses two modes: divergent thinking generates possibilities, and convergent thinking narrows them to the strongest. You can now tell the two apart, see why generating should come before judging, and choose the mode that fits the stage you are at. The next lesson looks at the barriers that stop this working, and how to move past them.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do that let the ideas flow?

items.text: She generated a list of drills first, without judging, then chose afterwards.
She started writing the plan straight away and judged each choice.
She spent the whole time reworking one drill.
She waited for a single good drill to arrive.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara generated first and judged second, keeping the two modes apart.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the move that separated generating from judging.
feedback.incorrectFinal: The ideas flowed because Amara generated a list first and judged afterwards. Writing straight away, reworking one drill, or waiting for one idea all collapse the two modes together.
